title: Quick qualitative pass on candidate Isabela Ramos
body:
Quick pass after the loop — rough/reflexive notes for syncing with Rae before we finalize. Don’t treat these as the canonical score; I was scribbling after each panel and flagged things to probe on reference calls.

Context / role fit
- Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (inference serving) — looking for someone to own latency-sensitive kernel decisions, follow high-throughput troubleshooting, and drive small infra improvements.
- Candidate background: 6 years infra + ML infra experience, last two years focused on model serving at a mid-size startup. Strong systems knowledge, some ML/attention familiarity but not an applied researcher.

Green flags (high signal)
- Operational instincts: immediately asked about tail latency sources and SLOs; brought up queuing effects in batching and how cold-starts interact with KV cache miss patterns. That’s exactly the mindset we need.
- Pragmatic debugging examples: two concrete incidents where she narrowed an issue from 150ms latency spikes to a mis-sized batcher shim and then changed backpressure config. Walked through steps, measurements, and how she validated the rollback under load.
- Communication: clear explainer style — can write runbooks and pair with SREs.

Neutral / mixed signals
- Quant work: comfortable reading quantization papers at a surface level; has limited hands-on experience with 4-bit/8-bit quantized inference pipelines. Knows the terminology and tradeoffs but hasn’t tuned kernels herself. Could ramp but not immediate kernel-level contributor.
- Distributed systems depth: good practical experience; smaller scale than our production environment (10s -> 100s of GPUs). Has ideas about sharding and routing but less exposure to cross-region active-active setups.

Concerns / red flags (moderate)
- Limited exposure to model compilation toolchains (TVM/XLA-like): when asked about compiler passes and kernel selection tradeoffs she answered at a conceptual level but couldn't enumerate concrete transformations she'd use to reduce memory bandwidth.
- Some risk-averse defaults: tends to prefer conservative rollouts and manual checkpoints; might slow down rapid experimentation we need in early staging unless coached.

Behavioral notes
- Team collaboration: referenced mentoring two junior infra engineers and one ML infra intern — provided examples of onboarding and runbooks she authored. Positive signal for cross-team enablement.
- Priorities & values: emphasizes reliability and clarity over micro-optimizations. Good cultural fit for SRE-heavy teams; may need encouragement to take ownership of product-level tradeoffs that accept small regressive costs for big UX wins.

Calibration (how to interpret the 6/10)
- Strengths give high operational value: we would see immediate improvement in on-call runbooks, incident mitigation, and batch/backpressure tuning.
- Weaknesses mean ramp time to be a core inference optimizer (kernel/compiler-level) is nontrivial (~3-6 months depending on shadowing and pairing with research/compilation team).

Suggested follow-ups if we move forward
- Short technical homework: ask her to profile a small transformer (local toy model) showing where token-latency comes from and propose 2-3 mitigations with cost/latency tradeoffs. Keeps scope practical and tests synthesis of system+model tradeoffs.
- Reference questions: explicitly ask previous manager about exposure to kernel-level debugging and whether she had opportunities to instrument low-level GPU paths.
- Pairing session: schedule a 60–90min pair with someone from the compilation/serving team (Devon or Mia) to do live profiling and to observe problem decomposition.

Notes for hiring committee
- Role mapping: fits a "Senior Production Engineer (inference ops)" better than a "Runtime Kernel Lead". If we have an opening for production-first senior engineer she could be prioritized.
- Compensation / leveling: mid-to-senior (L4/L5), probably needs a pump on low-level inference pay if we want her to cover kernel work long-term.

Action items (my recommendation)
- Sync with Rae and decide whether to keep moving: I’m inclined to invite the pairing session and homework rather than pass immediately. She has the right instincts and communication; the remaining unknowns are growthable.
- Draft reference email template (short): 1) confirm extent of kernel/compiler involvement, 2) probe examples of independent performance wins, 3) ask about on-call behavior and escalations.

Random scribbles / TODOs for my follow-up
- Capture a one-pager homework prompt that limits scope to a single-node profiling task.
- If we go ahead, schedule pairing in next 4 business days.
- Ask recruitment to nudge candidate on availability and shipping a short coding artifact (not full take-home).

-- Keaton
